angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 33,310,116 km at 164.75 pc = 2.7 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 204867: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 6.07 +/- 0.22 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 164.745 +/- 5.971 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 5.9728 +/- 0.2147 mas (same row, RUWE 3.08), 27.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 47.88 +/- 1.81 solar radii from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 204867: radius 47.88 +1.81/-1.68 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 2.704 +/- 0.009 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 33,310,116 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 4.97 +/- 0.1 solar masses from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 204867: mass 4.97 +/- 0.1 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5608 +/- 71 K from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 204867: effective temperature 5608 +/- 71 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 204867: effective temperature 5608 +/- 71 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/sadalsuud.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 1.774, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * bet Aqr: spectral type G0Ib (1989ApJS...71..245K)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * bet Aqr: projected rotation speed 8.74 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2025A&A...704A..49B)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 204867) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
